cast.name: Ines Varrow
cast.role: Stage manager and prompter of Pask's Players, thirty-four. The player character.
cast.want: To get the company to the end of the circuit fed, paid and together.
cast.flaw: Believes she is not an artist, and hides behind the prompt book so she never has to say what she thinks a scene means.
cast.voice: Lists, cue calls, flat understatement. 'Two minutes. If you are going to be sick, be sick stage left.'
cast.battle: The Prompter. Takes no role; feeds lines from the wings (buffs, turn order), and can go on in any role with the book in her hand at a penalty.
cast.secret: She was a regimental signaller on the crown's side. The order the play is about went down the line through her hands.

cast.name: Aurelio Pask
cast.role: Actor-manager and leading man, sixty. The company carries his name.
cast.want: One more great house before his voice goes.
cast.flaw: Can only play a part the way he has always played it.
cast.voice: Grand, wounded, misquotes the classics. 'As the poet says, the readiness is... most of it.'
cast.battle: Enormous in the Tyrant, a liability in anything else. His power scales with applause and collapses in silence.
cast.secret: He played the licensed version at court for six years and still draws the pension.

cast.name: Mother Clew
cast.role: Wardrobe mistress, seventy. Sews, mends and remembers everybody's lines.
cast.want: To see the play done word for word, once, in the right place.
cast.flaw: Would rather it be beautiful than accurate. In her text the rebels are saints.
cast.voice: Pins in her mouth. Short, practical, never answers the question asked. 'Hold this. No, taut.'
cast.battle: Costume. Changes a role's properties between acts; can sew two roles into one for a single scene.
cast.secret: She is Dessa Marl, who wrote the play and is supposed to have been hanged for it.

cast.name: Fenn
cast.role: Apprentice, seventeen. Plays the Fool and every part with fewer than ten lines.
cast.want: To find out what happened to their mother at Callow Ford.
cast.flaw: Believes whichever version they saw last.
cast.voice: Questions, one after another, deadpan. 'Why would she book us? Is that good? It doesn't feel good.'
cast.battle: Quick-change. The only actor who can swap roles in the middle of a scene.
cast.secret: They were seven and at the Ford that night, and what they remember matches none of the three versions.

cast.name: Corvin Hale
cast.role: Licenser of the Revels Office, assigned to ride with the company and approve each performance.
cast.want: To finish the circuit with nothing on his record.
cast.flaw: A frustrated critic. Cannot stop giving notes on a play he is supposed to be suppressing.
cast.voice: Fussy, formal, passionate about metre. 'I am striking the line. I also think it has a foot too many.'
cast.battle: The Blue Pencil. Strikes an enemy's line (silence) or one of yours. Joins the party as the Messenger once he stops pretending he does not want to.
cast.secret: His reports to the capital have been getting shorter and kinder since the second town.

cast.name: Hesper Vane
cast.role: The lead who ran off with the takings; now first lady of the Crown's Company, touring the approved Reconciliation Masque one town behind you.
cast.want: A theatre with a roof and a company that can afford rehearsals.
cast.flaw: Would rather be good than right.
cast.voice: Quick, amused, unkind in a way that is usually accurate. 'Darling, you were on book. In a bucket.'
cast.battle: Rival performer. Steals the audience's mood rather than attacking the cast.
cast.secret: She took the takings to pay the fine that kept Pask out of prison, and has never told him.

cast.name: Sir Anselm Dray
cast.role: Master of the Revels. Licenses every play in the kingdom. Commanded the crown's line at Callow Ford.
cast.want: For the war to be over, which to him means nobody mentioning it.
cast.voice: Courteous, tired, never raises it. 'I have read your play. I thought the second act rather hard on everyone.'
cast.battle: Does not fight. He closes theatres, withdraws licences and buys the front row.
cast.secret: The order was his, it was three words long, and he sent it twice.

places.name: The Wagon
places.look: Two carts, a folding stage, a costume trunk that is older than the war, washing on the prop rail.
places.play: Cast roles, rehearse scenes (which is how skills level), mend costumes, and hold the camp conversations.
places.change: The cast list on the tailboard gets crossed out and rewritten until it is mostly Ines's handwriting.

places.name: Pellam Barn
places.look: A tithe barn with hay bales for a gallery and swallows in the roof.
places.play: The first performance. A forgiving house that teaches the audience meter.
places.change: By the end they have put on the play themselves, badly, with a pig as the Tyrant.

places.name: The Dark House at Marrow
places.look: A playhouse that burned on the last night before the war. The last performance is still running inside without its actors.
places.play: Fight the Uncast, roles with nobody in them, and recover the missing third act from the prompt corner.
places.change: Once you have played its final scene through to the end, it is only a ruin.

places.name: Greywether
places.look: A garrison town of slate and whitewash. The playhouse is the drill hall with the musket racks pushed back.
places.play: Perform for three hundred soldiers who were at the Ford. The hardest house on the circuit.
places.change: The regiment starts holding its own evening on the anniversary, with no officers invited.

places.name: Saltmarket
places.look: A rich port. The Rose-and-Anchor has gilt boxes, a flying rig and a real sea that floods the pit for the finale.
places.play: Share a bill with the Crown's Company and compete for the same audience over three nights.
places.change: Whichever company loses the house plays the inn yard afterwards.

places.name: The Revels Office
places.look: A library of every play ever licensed, shelved with every play ever refused, which is the larger collection.
places.play: A stealth-and-paperwork dungeon. Find the Callow Ford file, and the forty other scripts with the same hand's corrections.
places.change: What is on its shelves at the end depends on what you carried out.

places.name: Callow Ford
places.look: A mill, a rebuilt street that stops halfway, and a meadow where the playhouse was. Nobody has put anything on it.
places.play: The last performance, on bare grass, for the people it happened to.
places.change: The meadow gets a stage, a stone, or nothing, depending on the play you gave it.
